title: The Oracle
corpus_scope: ICLR 2026 · 19,474 reviewed papers with a primary area · association, not destiny
question: Does a paper's field predict how it will be criticized?

figures.title: The archipelago: all twenty-one primary areas, drawn as a sea chart
figures.deck: Fields criticized alike drift together — and each island's coastline is its fingerprint: learning theory's theory cape rises +25pp above the venue while its baselines shore falls away −31pp.

claims.statement: Every paper carries a primary area, so the criticism profiles can be split by field without any further modelling — 19,474 reviewed papers with a primary area in all.
claims.derivation: sum of n across all 21 primary-area islands

claims.statement: Learning theory's theory cape rises +25pp above the venue while its baselines shore falls away −31pp.
claims.derivation: dev[theory] = 0.2541 → +25.4pp above the venue baseline; dev[baselines_ablations] = −0.3051 → −30.5pp, rounding to −31pp

claims.statement: Learning theory sits far offshore with a great cape toward theory and a deep bay where its baselines shore should be.
claims.derivation: multidimensional-scaling placement (x,y) of the learning-theory island, driven by its dev[] vector relative to the other 20 islands

claims.statement: Datasets & benchmarks — the island least judged by theory anywhere on the chart — anchors the southwest alone.
claims.derivation: lowest dev[theory] value across all 21 islands, combined with its (x,y) MDS placement

caveats.text: Conditional frequencies only: fields differ in what they submit as much as in how they are judged. The chart encodes association, not destiny.
caveats.scope: all Plate XXVIII field-vs-venue and archipelago claims
